candidates.name: Paulskirche
candidates.content: A church with important political symbolism in Germany. This was the seat of the first democratically elected parliament in Germany in 1848. Here the revolutionaries wrote the 1848 constitution that sadly was never put into effect

candidates.name: Museum für Moderne Kunst
candidates.content: The building was designed by Hans Hollein to resemble a boat, which is most notable when approaching it from the back (east). Apart from well-known artists in the permanent collection, e.g. Roy Liechtenstein and Andy Warhol, the m

candidates.name: Naturmuseum Senckenberg
candidates.content: Commonly called just Senckenberg museum it is one of the most famous museums in Frankfurt. The Senckenberg has various exhibits on natural history; plants, animals, minerals, and so on; the biggest attraction are the dinosaur skel

candidates.name: Römerberg
candidates.content: Römerberg is the historic centre of Frankfurt, with a number of beautiful buildings, including the town hall and a church from the 14th and 15th century. The name Römer itself refers to the town hall of Frankfurt, which itself rec

candidates.name: Dom-Römer-Areal
candidates.content: Urban revitalization of the Dom-Römer complex, in which a number of old historic buildings have been rebuilt from scratch – incorporating only a few original artifacts – based on old pictures and drawings. The area includes the St

candidates.name: St. Leonhardskirche
candidates.content: Late Romanic church built in 1219, and transformed in accordance with the Gothic style in the 15th century. English-language Catholic mass service on Saturdays and Sundays.

candidates.name: Kunsthalle Schirn
candidates.price: Ticket prices vary depending on the exhibitions
candidates.content: A museum specializing in contemporary art. It is located just off the Römerplatz. There are two exhibition spaces that rotate every month or two.

candidates.name: Archäologisches Museum
candidates.price: Adults €7, reduced €3.50, under 18 years free, free entry every last Saturday of the month
candidates.content: In a building which used to house a Carmelite monastery.

candidates.name: Historisches Museum
candidates.content: Historic museum of the city of Frankfurt and its citizens. Today it offers a wide collection of the history of the city.

candidates.name: Caricatura Museum for Comic Art
candidates.content: Museum for comic art, i.e., satire and illustrations. Located in the old Leinwandhaus (Linen House), a historic building that was first constructed in 1396–1399, but only reopened in 1984 after suffering substantial damage in Worl

candidates.name: Palais Thurn und Taxis
candidates.content: 18th-century palace of the Princely House of Thurn and Taxis. In the 19th century, it served as the parliament of the German Confederation. Unfortunately, apart from the front façade, most of it is reconstructed. The reconstructio

candidates.name: Katharinenkirche
candidates.content: Baroque-style Lutheran church at Hauptwache. Constructed 1678 to 1681 at the site of a former monastery, destroyed during World War II, and restored 1950 to 1954. The tower stands tall.

candidates.name: Goethe-Haus und -Museum
candidates.content: Birthplace of Johann Wolfgang von Goethe, Germany's most famous author and poet. It's a museum and picture gallery devoted to Goethe.

candidates.name: Bornheim
candidates.content: A nice residential quarter with a lively market and beautiful medieval houses which survived the war intact (unlike the city centre). The most important and lively street is the Berger Straße, which runs from downtown all the way

candidates.name: Dialogmuseum
candidates.content: Experience the world as blind people do. Guided tour through rooms in complete darkness, led by blind or visually impaired staff members. In each room, you experience a different daily life situation (e.g., walking through a park,

candidates.name: Liebfrauenkirche
candidates.content: 14th century Roman Catholic church and monastery.

candidates.name: Börse Frankfurt
candidates.content: The Frankfurt stock exchange building, still in use, see the bull and bear statues just outside. You cannot enter the building unless you have registered for a guided tour at least one working day in advance.

candidates.name: Main Tower
candidates.content: This building is special as it is the only Frankfurt high-rise tower that is open to the public with an elevator to the viewing platform at a height of . From here, you will have a good view of Frankfurt and the surrounding area.

candidates.name: Experiminta
candidates.content: Interactive science museum focusing on hands-on exhibits.

candidates.name: Anne Frank Educational Center
candidates.hours: Sat Sun 12:00-18:00, Mon-Fri closed (exceptions for groups with appointment)
candidates.content: The well-known young Holocaust victim Anne Frank was born in Frankfurt and first lived with her family in a house at Marbachweg 307, just minutes away from this centre, before they moved to Ganghofer Straße 24, which is a few bloc

candidates.name: Portikus
candidates.hours: Tue-Fri 12:00-18:00, Sat Sun 11:00-19:00, also closed when there is no current exhibition and on some public holidays
candidates.content: An institution exhibiting contemporary art of emerging and established artists. It was founded in 1987 and is part of the Städelschule (Staatliche Hochschule für Bildende Künste, a school of art).

candidates.name: Höchst Old Town
candidates.content: The old town of Höchst with its castle and small medieval streets full of half-timbered houses.

candidates.name: Eiserner Steg
candidates.content: Relatively well-known bridge for pedestrians, built in 1869. It is just a minute away from the Römer. Crossing the bridge leads you to Sachsenhausen and provides good views of the skyline.

candidates.name: Staufenmauer
candidates.content: Remains of the old city wall (1138–1254) can be seen in the Fahrgasse and at the Liebfrauenkirche. More prominent examples of the city fortification built in later years include the Eschenheimer Turm (1428) near Hauptwache and the

candidates.name: Hauptwache
candidates.content: A public area that is often considered the central hub of Frankfurt's modern downtown area due to its importance as a public transportation station and its central location, right between the main shopping street (Zeil) and the Ro

candidates.name: Alte Oper
candidates.content: Renaissance Opera Building in the centre of the city. A busy square with fountains can be found in front of it. It was opened in 1880, but it has not been used for operas since the rebuilding after the war, but for concerts, congr

candidates.name: Palmengarten
candidates.content: The Palmengarten is one of two botanical gardens in Frankfurt. There are special exhibitions and events throughout the much of the year.

candidates.name: Grüneburgpark
candidates.content: This is Frankfurt's largest public park. Even though there are many parks in Frankfurt, the Grüneburgpark is probably the most liked. It is close to two campuses of the university: many young people meet there, and many business p

candidates.name: Johann Wolfgang Goethe University
candidates.content: Founded in 1914, this urban university offers a wide range of faculties. Today, the university has 38,000 students on 4 major campuses: Campus Bockenheim, Campus Riedberg, Campus Westend, Campus Niederrad.

candidates.name: River cruises along the Main River
candidates.content: There are two companies offering river cruises along the Main River, and both of them depart from Mainkai near the Eiserner Steg bridge in the Old Town. There are short sightseeing cruises as well as longer tours heading towards t

candidates.name: Volkshochschule Frankfurt
candidates.content: Vast range of language courses, cooking classes and other educational courses.

candidates.name: Oper Frankfurt
candidates.content: Not to be confused with the historic Alte Oper building, this modern building is where to go to see an opera performance. State subsidized performances make this a relatively affordable place to see high quality productions

candidates.name: Lohrberg
candidates.content: Head up the Lohrberg, where you can enjoy beautiful views of the city, as well as of the local vineyard (the last remaining one in Frankfurt). There is a small restaurant with outdoor seating and an apple orchard serving homemade

candidates.name: Eintracht Frankfurt
candidates.content: Die Adler (The Eagles) play football (soccer) in Bundesliga, the top tier. The stadium (sponsored as Deutsche Bank Park) has a capacity of 51,500, and in 2024 it hosted games in the UEFA Euro Finals. The women's team play in their

candidates.name: Bockenheimer Depot
candidates.content: A theatre venue of the Städtische Bühnen Frankfurt, for opera and dance performances.

candidates.name: Ice skating ring
candidates.content: Ice skating for amateurs or watch ice hockey games by the local teams.

candidates.name: Boulderwelt Frankfurt
candidates.content: Opened in the winter of 2012, this hall is still expanding and has boulders in various difficulties for beginners to experienced ones. The route setter is very experienced and the crew friendly. Only the air can get "powdry" at pe

candidates.name: The Dresden Frankfurt Dance Company
candidates.content: Modern ballet in Frankfurt playing at the Bockenheimer Depot.

candidates.name: Goethe Institut
candidates.content: The official German language institute with a vast range of courses to learn German in Goethe's hometown.

candidates.name: Cinestar Metropolis
candidates.content: The cinema shows a couple of movies in English.

candidates.name: Dynochrom
candidates.content: This gym has tough boulders for enthusiastic climbers.

candidates.name: Kobelt-Zoo
candidates.content: A small zoo with monkeys, snakes and other animals. Kids can pet rabbits, horses, donkeys, and goats, or ride ponies.

candidates.name: Sportpark Kelkheim
candidates.content: A sports facility complex that features high rope courses, golf (no membership required), indoor climbing and bouldering, squash, and other activities.

candidates.name: English theatre
candidates.content: See a play at the largest English-language theatre in continental Europe

candidates.name: Kletterzentrum Frankfurt/Main
candidates.content: The DAV Kletterzentrum opened for climbing in spring 2013. It offers up to high walls with many routes.

candidates.name: Gibson Club
candidates.content: The Gibson club has a chic and urban atmosphere. They have both live and DJ acts. It opened in spring 2012. The long lines outside the nightclub move fast.

candidates.name: Zoom
candidates.content: Jazz, Reggae, Dancehall and Rock club for the middle aged (30-50 yr) with special guests and regular themes. It is the successor of the Sinkkasten artsclub and attracts many indie-bands.

candidates.name: Die Rote Bar
candidates.content: This cocktail bar offers excellent drinks in a stylish atmosphere. The bar has its own whiskey selection. Better be well dressed for the door. Coming late, one has to wait a bit outside until space is found inside.

candidates.name: Cafe & Bar Celona
candidates.content: Daily 09:00-01:00, F Sa 09:00-02:00. Spanish-style bar in the heart of the city. Popular, attracts a younger crowd, good for meeting people. Very crowded around 17:00-19:00. Also serves a variety of Spanish dishes. €7-20/person.

candidates.name: Club Voltaire
candidates.content: Since 1962 exists this cultural tavern. It offers drinks for mixed public of all ages. Sometimes it asks for entry for the musicians or lecturers, but generally it is free entry.

candidates.name: Hoppenworth & Ploch
candidates.content: The student café is serving and selling excellent espressos. They are proud about their barrista knowledge. The room is not only flooded by the many students of the campus, but by excellent café flavour and electronic music. They

candidates.name: Tanzhaus West
candidates.content: The club is mostly known for drum and bass music. It has a relaxed public. The website has details on the performing artists. During summertime the back is open also on Sundays for relaxing with good music.

candidates.name: Robert Johnson
candidates.content: They don't announce who is playing for that one has to subscribe to the monthly newsletter to know. It is usual playing minimal electronic music. The club has a terrace and beautiful view over the main. The sound system is refined

candidates.name: Wacker´s Kaffee Geschäft
candidates.content: Since 1914 known for its good coffee. Very packed over lunch time but has its own roast of coffee. Don't mind a long queue, the crew is dedicated and you will never wait more than five minutes for your coffee

candidates.name: Volkswirtschaft
candidates.content: It streams important football matches. The tavern is usually very packed.

candidates.name: Jazzkeller
candidates.content: Since 1952 the Jazz meeting point. Outstanding Jazz music for everyone with special concerts once in a while.

candidates.name: Velvet Club
candidates.content: Club in downtown Frankfurt with very nice interior design. Great place for house and electronic music lovers.

candidates.name: Sandbar
candidates.content: This place has small snacks and good wines.

candidates.name: Batschkapp
candidates.content: The place for rock and alternative music. One of the oldest clubs in town (since 1976). The club moved enthusiastically to the new place in 2013.

candidates.name: Best Worscht in Town
candidates.content: Place where you can try "Curry-Wurst", which is a sliced beef sausage served with ketchup and curry spices, and considered one of the most popular German fast food products. The Best Worscht in Town chain is special in that it als

candidates.name: Ruchi
candidates.content: A very short walk north from the main train station you find daily Indian all-you-can-eat tasty buffet and at a good value. South Indian buffet on Saturdays. Idly, dosas, vada, pani puri, Manchurian, and bajjis are all available.

candidates.name: Zum Alten Frankfurter
candidates.content: It feels like a family run place. Intimate and quiet. Food freshly cooked with passion. Schnitzel: the breading throws bubbles the way it should be. The service charming and quick. All in all a nice experience.

candidates.name: Tonbul Grill und Kebap Haus
candidates.content: Delicious "homemade" doner kebab with a unique touch. Not a standard kebab. Super nice place with homemade fresh products. The sauces are very yummy. The staff is also very friendly.

candidates.name: Paulaner am Dom
candidates.content: Traditional Bavarian restaurant, perhaps a bit touristy, right behind the cathedral near Römer. It's difficult to get a table at weekends without a reservation.

candidates.name: Ristorante Punto e Pasta 1998
candidates.content: A really friendly little pizzeria. Hidden behind the main train station. The pizzas are really tasty, crispy crust, thin dough and aromatic topping. Good traditional Italian service.

candidates.name: Emma Metzler
candidates.hours: Tue-Sat 12:00–23:00, Sun 12:00–18:00, kitchen has limited hours: Tue-Sat 12:00–14:00 and 18:00–22:00, Sun 12:00–15:00
candidates.content: A relaxed international-local cuisine with great service and changing menu. Set in the Bauhaus-Style Museum für Angewandte Kunst (Museum of Applied Arts), close to the Main river, but with no view. Quite recommendable. Suitable fo

candidates.name: Lahmer Esel
candidates.content: Expands in summer time over to tables in the garden. It has local authentic food to fair prices and good fresh quality. It is popular as after dinner from the Frankfurt Goethe University faculty. The local "Apfelwein" (Ebbelwoi) i

candidates.name: Speisekammer
candidates.hours: 17:00- during summer, 18:00- winter, Sun lunch too
candidates.content: This traditional place has an idyllic garden with very old trees. The food is typical and very regional, nevertheless it has many options for vegetarians. The present by the house adds to the stylish environment of a pleasureable

candidates.name: China Garten
candidates.content: If you want to eat quality and tasty Asian food and that at great prices, you have to go here. The service is always very friendly.

candidates.name: Strahmann Baguetterie & Cafébar
candidates.content: the best focaccias in town! Also they have a huge variety of other sandwiches, salads, snacks etc. Sometimes the queue is long.

candidates.name: Pizzeria 7 Bello
candidates.content: Good lunch option for fast pizza and pasta. Popular during summer as they have a small terrace on the side walk.

candidates.name: Fahrradhaus Wagner
candidates.content: The small shop at the outskirts of Frankfurt has a long tradition since 1929 selling bikes. One can see their passion for bikes in how well they keep the records of their sold bikes and repairs. The prices are really fair and the

candidates.name: Kleinmarkthalle
candidates.hours: Mon-Fri 08:00-18:00, Sat 08:00-16:00, Sun and holidays closed
candidates.content: A market hall with a large variety of local and international vendors ranging from fresh produce to ready-to-eat food and drinks.

candidates.name: Farmer's Market at Konstablerwache
candidates.content: Locally produced vegetables or fruits are found also directly from regional ecological producers.

candidates.name: Schillermarkt
candidates.content: Fresh meals and local products are sold at the groceries market directly in the centre at this shopping street.

candidates.name: Flea Market
candidates.content: Along the river in Sachsenhausen during which time the road is normally closed to traffic.

december.text: Ice skating: The Eissporthalle Frankfurt offers multiple indoor and outdoor ice rinks. The indoor rink is available all year round but the outdoor ones are only available during the winter. Ice skate rental and lockers are available inside.

Bethmännchen – A pastry made mainly from marzipan and almonds. Popular during Christmas time.
Ice skating ring: Ice skating for amateurs or watch ice hockey games by the local teams.
